selected_evidence.requirement: Every sudo command logged to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user and timestamp
selected_evidence.summary: sudoers.d drop-in created and validated (visudo parsed OK); sudo-commands.log then shows entries like 'Sep 4 23:15:24 2026 : root : PWD=/ ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/bin/whoami' with full timestamp, user, and command.

selected_evidence.requirement: Sudo command entries kept out of the general system log (/var/log/secure)
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline showed sudo COMMAND= lines in /var/log/secure before the change; after installing the !syslog / logfile sudoers Defaults, new sudo invocations (whoami, id, cat) no longer produced COMMAND= entries in /var/log/secure -- only generic PAM session open/close lines remained there.

selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline health capture prior to restart (node1)
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id fb2aa416-d036-46d3-aeb8-30c65a01cb34, confirmed sudoers.d file present, rsyslog active, and log had 20 entries before reboot.
systemctl reboot issued in background with disown; command stream closed as node1 began shutting down, confirming the reboot was accepted and executing.

selected_evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed after restart
selected_evidence.summary: After polling through connection timeouts/resets, exec access returned with boot_id 09b5da90-1817-400e-9c89-08300ef0be11, differing from the pre-restart fb2aa416-d036-46d3-aeb8-30c65a01cb34, proving a genuine reboot.

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of sudo command logging and cluster/service state on node1
selected_evidence.summary: After reboot, sudoers.d/95-sudo-command-logging still present, rsyslog active, and new sudo commands (whoami, tail) appended correctly-formatted entries to sudo-commands.log (25 lines, up from 20) while /var/log/secure tail showed no COMMAND= lines for them -- confirming the logging behavior survived the restart.
